text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- A pack of cigarettes will cost some 20 centimes more starting March 1997 when the Swiss government raises tobacco taxes.
- The Swiss government says it is ready to start an investment programme worth 700 million Swiss francs in order to boost the country's economy.
- Switzerland has again decided to reduce unemployment payments effective January 1.
- Company bankruptcies in Switzerland rose by 9.6 percent by the end of November compared to the same period the year before.
- Elektrowatt AG's board of directors wants to pay out a dividend of 16 percent or eight Swiss francs per share for the eight months of 1996 from February 1 to September 30.

- Though Switzerland's Israeli Community chose 54-year-old historian Urs Altermatt to be president of the independent expert commission investigating Switzerland's role in Nazi gold and funds of Holocaust victims, Altermatt declined because the government did not completely support him.
- The European Union Commission okayed the European-wide cultivation and import of Ciba Geigy's genetically manipulated maize.
- The number of Swiss Yellow Berets helping in Bosnia will be reduced from 50 to 30.
